name: Sesbania

project_scope.selection_mode: GENUS GITHUB BACKFILL from approved Master Plant Pool; no species installation

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Find an alternate, EVEN-pinnate leaf with paired narrow leaflets and an axillary raceme of pea-type flowers. If fruit is present, inspect the WHOLE pod in profile and cross-section: four papery wings and a short stout pod versus a very long, slender, nearly cylindrical pod. Pods are the best first species split.
shared_traits: Fabaceae plants with alternate, even-pinnately compound leaves; many paired entire-margined leaflets along a single rachis, often folding by nighttime movement.
Pea-type (papilionaceous) flowers with banner, paired wings and keel; ten stamens usually in a 9+1 arrangement; racemes arise in leaf axils.
Superior one-carpel ovaries that mature into legumes, but pod cross-section, dimensions, seed count and dehiscence differ strongly between the two study species.
shared_genus_recognition.caution: A leaf full of small paired leaflets is not species-level evidence, nor is flower color. Look for mature, attached fruits or reproductive racemes with scale.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: entire fruit attached to a flowering/fruiting branch; side and end views
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Short, broad, four-winged papery pod -> S. drummondii candidate; very long, pencil-thin nearly cylindrical pod -> S. herbacea candidate.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: whole axillary raceme with individual flowers counted
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Many-flowered pendent raceme, often 12+ flowers -> S. drummondii; shorter, usually 2–6-flowered raceme -> S. herbacea (variable and supporting only).

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: leaf rachis and leaflet pairs, plus woody basal stem/annual root if visible
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Drummondii often ~11–19 leaflet pairs on a leaf to ~23 cm; herbacea can have much longer leaves to ~46 cm and many more leaflet pairs. Size overlaps; do not diagnose from one leaf.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: unripe pods, atypical stems, or leaf-only evidence
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Leave Sesbania sp. until fruit shape or a full flower-plus-leaf voucher confirms the split.

species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania drummondii: Woody-based shrub with ascending branches, typically ~1.2–3.5 m tall in Williamson County description.
species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania herbacea: Robust taprooted annual herb in moist or wet substrate, ~0.5–4 m tall; lower older stem can become fibrous/partly woody.

species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania drummondii: Even-pinnate leaves to ~230 mm, (5–)11–19 paired leaflets; leaflets often ~20–44 × up to 13 mm.
species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania herbacea: Very long even-pinnate leaves to ~460 mm; may bear many pairs, with up to 107 lateral leaflets; leaflets usually ~18–35(–50) × 2.2–9.3 mm.
species_comparison_matrix.weight: supporting; inspect several fully expanded leaves

species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania drummondii: Usually numerous flowers, often 12+ in an axillary raceme.
species_comparison_matrix.weight: strong supporting when mature; population variability expected

species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania drummondii: Distinctly four-angled/four-winged flattened legume with papery wings; often dark brown.
species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania herbacea: Nearly cylindrical slender legume without conspicuous four papery wings.

species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania drummondii: Typically ~42–80 mm long × 10 mm wide; stalk often 15+ mm.
species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania herbacea: Typically ~150–210+ mm long × 3.3–3.8 mm wide; short stalk often <4 mm.

species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania drummondii: Indehiscent four-winged pods commonly containing ~2–7 larger seeds.
species_comparison_matrix.Sesbania herbacea: Pod opens by two sutures at maturity; many regularly spaced seeds, commonly ~30–35.

field_teaching_cautions: Fruit anatomy outranks leaf size, flower color, stature and wet-ground habitat. Pods should be mature and attached to a confidently associated plant.
The four papery pod wings of S. drummondii are not ordinary leaf wings. Photograph pod edges and cross section with a ruler.
Old S. herbacea stems can form tough woody fibers; stem woodiness alone is not a reliable perennial-versus-annual test.
Leaflets can fold due to nyctinasty or handling; photograph fully spread leaves for counts and measurements.
Rattlebush seeds are poisonous: never taste seeds or use plant parts as food.
Approved-source-pool presence supports a genus lesson; neither taxon becomes canonical or target-zone PASS from this file.

local_lookalikes.separate: Inspect the mature pod: joint-vetch pods have distinctly segmented/loment-like fruits, not the Sesbania four-winged or very long cylindrical pod. Confirm stem and floral structure.
Check spikes of small reduced-wing/keel flowers versus full papilionoid Sesbania flowers, and very different short one- or few-seeded pods.
Mimosa has bipinnate foliage and heads of tiny flowers with conspicuous stamens, not the simple even-pinnate leaf and pea-type raceme of Sesbania.

local_lookalikes.group: Glottidium vesicarium / historical Sesbania vesicaria (encounter comparison where present)
local_lookalikes.separate: Compare an inflated or bladdery shorter legume against four-winged S. drummondii and long narrow S. herbacea; do not infer local range without records.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: full pod with millimeter ruler and arrows to four papery wings vs cylindrical thin profile; attach source species name
four wing tips on drummondii; circular-to-elliptical slender herbacea; dehiscent margins noted

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: whole axillary raceme on leafy branch
diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: axillary origin, flower count and raceme orientation
leaf length, rachis, many opposite leaflet pairs, node and stipules; avoid folded leaves
one dissected flower, each structure individually labeled
whole shrub vs robust annual, basal branching and wet-substrate context
